name: Deckers Brands

logo.source: en.wikipedia.org infobox logo (Deckers Brands logo.png (340x96 px; no SVG found))

description: Deckers owns footwear brands and makes money by designing them and having contract factories build them. HOKA (running and outdoor shoes, 47 percent of FY2026 sales) and UGG (sheepskin boots and casual footwear, 50 percent) do almost all the business; Teva and the smaller brands are 3 percent. About 60 percent of sales go to retailers and distributors (wholesale) and about 40 percent through its own websites and stores. FY2026 net sales were $5.47 billion (+9.8%) with a 23.1 percent operating margin and $1.02 billion net income; HOKA grew 15.9 percent and UGG 8.2 percent while the other brands fell about a third.

sub.name: Fashion, footwear, beauty and leisure brands

gics.note: Wikipedia list gives only sector and sub-industry; industry group and industry were not in a source read, so left null.

employees.note: About 6,000 global employees, including about 2,200 in retail stores (FY2026 10-K)

businessLines.name: UGG
businessLines.how: Sells boots and slippers at full price through its own sites and stores and to retailers; strongly seasonal (autumn and winter) and a fashion cycle risk, but the highest segment margin.
businessLines.description: UGG brand footwear, apparel and accessories (also Koolaburra by UGG)

businessLines.name: HOKA
businessLines.how: Sells running shoes mostly wholesale to specialty running and sporting-goods retailers (64 percent of the brand) and the rest direct; growth comes from new retail doors, DTC and international expansion.
businessLines.description: HOKA performance running, trail and lifestyle footwear and apparel

businessLines.name: Other brands
businessLines.how: Sandals and casual footwear sold mostly wholesale; small and shrinking.
